newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Monsanto seen keeping Searle unit.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Monsanto seen keeping Searle unit.

text.p: -- Natwest Securities said Monday it expects Monsanto Co to keep its G.D. Searle pharmaceutical unit, which analysts have expected the chemical and agribusiness company to sell.

-- "Searle is now likely a 'keeper.' We believe that Monsanto is unlikely to divest Searle as its impressive turnaround gains visibility and increases shareholder value," Natwest analysts said in a report.
-- Natwest has a hold rating on Monsanto, whose shares were up 1/2 at 32.
-- A Monsanto spokeswoman declined to comment on whether Searle has been for sale or if plans for the drug unit have changed, adding the company does not comment on speculation.

-- "The common wisdom among the Street's pharmaceutical analysts is that Searle is 'on the block' in a consolidating world pharmaceutical industry, where small players (like Searle) are at an increasing risk of being marginalized by the behemoths forming around them," Natwest said.
-- Natwest said it expects Monsanto to benefit from an ongoing, long-term earnings turnaround at Searle.

-- "In addition to the value currently being realized from Searle-developed technologies, we believe that Monsanto views Searle as a very valuable platform upon which to launch technologies...that Monsanto is developing in its other divisions," Natwest added.
-- Natwest noted that one promising drug in the Searle pipeline is the COX-2 inhibitor for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis.
